You are a research coordinator for an LLM agent research reading group. Your workspace contains paper_ids.txt with a list of eight arXiv paper IDs and Reading_Guidelines.md describing the reading group format and discussion expectations.

Your task is to create a structured reading plan for the group. Begin by retrieving paper metadata from the preprint repository for every paper ID listed in paper_ids.txt.

How the repository (the arXiv tools) works: it does NOT support a direct lookup by arXiv ID. It offers two relevant tools. One lists all papers currently stored in the repository and returns each paper's title and abstract. The other is a keyword search that matches on words in a paper's title and abstract and returns, for each match, the arXiv ID, title, authors, abstract, categories, and published date. Because the search matches on title/abstract text rather than the ID string, searching for an ID such as "2302.01560" will return nothing. Recommended flow: first list all stored papers to obtain their titles and abstracts, then for each paper run a keyword search using distinctive words from its title to retrieve the full metadata (published date and categories), and match the returned arXiv ID back to the corresponding entry in paper_ids.txt.

Then create an Excel file called Reading_Plan.xlsx in your workspace with two sheets. The first sheet must be named Papers and contain exactly eight rows (one per paper) with these columns: ArXiv_ID, Title, Authors (the full author list, comma-separated), Published_Date (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD), Category (the paper's primary arXiv category, e.g. cs.CL), Abstract_Summary (the first 100 characters of the abstract, exactly as returned by the repository), Assigned_Session (a number from 1 to 8 assigned in the order the papers appear in paper_ids.txt). The second sheet must be named Schedule and contain exactly eight rows (one per reading session) with these columns: Session_Number, Session_Date (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD), Paper_Count, Topics_Covered. Session 1 starts on Monday March 9, 2026 and each subsequent session is one week later. Each session covers one paper. Topics_Covered should be the abbreviated title or topic area of that session's paper.

Next, create eight events on the shared calendar, one for each reading session. Each event title must follow the pattern "Reading Session N: [abbreviated paper title]" where N is the session number. Schedule each event on the corresponding Monday starting from the Monday of the launch week, at 10:00 to 11:30 UTC. Include the full paper title and arXiv ID in the event description.

Finally, send an email from coordinator@lab.example.com to reading-group@lab.example.com. The subject must contain "LLM Agent Research Reading Plan". The body must mention the total number of papers, the date range covered by the reading sessions, and the names or topics of at least three of the eight papers.

When all outputs are produced, call claim_done.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly as the main agent without dispatching any sub-agents. Read paper_ids.txt and Reading_Guidelines.md read-only first, preserving the exact eight-ID source order, the session numbering, the Monday schedule, the UTC time and every workbook rule they define. For each paper, retrieve its metadata/abstract through the arXiv tools once, freezing literal titles/dates. Then, in one pass per deliverable: build the reading-plan workbook with the exact sheets/headers and one row per paper in source order; create each Monday reading-session calendar event exactly once with explicit UTC start/end (search exact summaries first and create only missing events, then read every retained ID back); and send the announcement email exactly once to the guideline-defined recipient/subject, paginating Sent search first and reading the retained message back. Reconcile the workbook rows, event count and sent message against the frozen eight-paper list, then call claim_done; do not add a separate verification phase.

You are a planning sub-agent for a research coordinator task. Decompose the following task into an ordered list of subtasks. For each subtask, specify: (a) the dispatch decision: `self` (main agent), `explore`, or `coder`; (b) whether it is independent/parallelizable or must wait for another subtask's output; (c) the concrete tool calls involved.

CONTEXT: The workspace is /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-reading-plan-excel-gcal-email/workspace. It contains paper_ids.txt (a list of eight arXiv paper IDs) and Reading_Guidelines.md (reading group format and discussion expectations).

THE TASK (from the user):
1. Retrieve paper metadata from an arXiv preprint repository for every paper ID in paper_ids.txt. The repository does NOT support lookup by arXiv ID. It offers:
   - `mcp__arxiv_local__list_papers`: lists all stored papers, returns each paper's title and abstract.
   - `mcp__arxiv_local__search_papers`: keyword search matching words in title/abstract; returns arXiv ID, title, authors, abstract, categories, published date. Searching an ID string returns nothing.
   Recommended flow: list all stored papers to get titles/abstracts, then for each paper run a keyword search using distinctive title words to get full metadata (published date, categories), and match the returned arXiv ID back to the corresponding entry in paper_ids.txt.
2. Create Excel file Reading_Plan.xlsx in the workspace with two sheets:
   - Sheet "Papers": exactly 8 rows, columns: ArXiv_ID, Title, Authors (full author list comma-separated), Published_Date (YYYY-MM-DD), Category (primary arXiv category e.g. cs.CL), Abstract_Summary (first 100 characters of the abstract, exactly as returned by the repository), Assigned_Session (number 1-8 in the order papers appear in paper_ids.txt).
   - Sheet "Schedule": exactly 8 rows, columns: Session_Number, Session_Date (YYYY-MM-DD), Paper_Count, Topics_Covered. Session 1 on Monday March 9, 2026; each subsequent session one week later; one paper per session. Topics_Covered = abbreviated title/topic area of that session's paper.
3. Create eight Google Calendar events (one per reading session). Title pattern: "Reading Session N: [abbreviated paper title]". Each event on the corresponding Monday (starting Monday of launch week = March 9, 2026), 10:00-11:30 UTC. Description must include full paper title and arXiv ID.
4. Send an email from coordinator@lab.example.com to reading-group@lab.example.com. Subject must contain "LLM Agent Research Reading Plan". Body must mention: total number of papers, date range covered by reading sessions, and names or topics of at least three of the eight papers.
5. Call mcp__local__claim_done when everything is done.

DELIVERABLE: Return the ordered subtask list with dispatch decisions and dependency/parallelism annotations, plus a validation checklist (how to verify each deliverable). Keep it concise and actionable.
Plan reading group task

You are creating an Excel reading plan workbook. Work only within /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-reading-plan-excel-gcal-email/workspace.

STEP 1: Read the staged metadata file at /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-reading-plan-excel-gcal-email/workspace/metadata.json. It is a JSON list of 8 objects, each with keys: assigned_session, arxiv_id, title, authors (already comma-separated full author list), published_date (YYYY-MM-DD), category (primary category), abstract, abstract_summary (exactly the first 100 characters of the abstract), abbreviated_title.

STEP 2: Create the Excel file at /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-reading-plan-excel-gcal-email/workspace/Reading_Plan.xlsx using the mcp__excel__ tools (create_workbook, create_worksheet, write_data_to_excel, rename_worksheet, delete_worksheet as needed). The workbook must contain exactly two sheets:

Sheet 1 named "Papers" — exactly 8 data rows (one per paper, in metadata.json order) with header row and these EXACT column names in this order:
ArXiv_ID | Title | Authors | Published_Date | Category | Abstract_Summary | Assigned_Session
- ArXiv_ID: the arxiv_id value
- Title: the title value
- Authors: the authors value (as-is)
- Published_Date: the published_date value (YYYY-MM-DD)
- Category: the category value (primary category, e.g. cs.CL)
- Abstract_Summary: the abstract_summary value EXACTLY (first 100 characters, do not modify)
- Assigned_Session: the assigned_session number (1-8)

Sheet 2 named "Schedule" — exactly 8 data rows with header row and these EXACT column names in this order:
Session_Number | Session_Date | Paper_Count | Topics_Covered
- Session_Number: 1 through 8
- Session_Date: Monday dates, one week apart: 2026-03-09, 2026-03-16, 2026-03-23, 2026-03-30, 2026-04-06, 2026-04-13, 2026-04-20, 2026-04-27 (formatted YYYY-MM-DD)
- Paper_Count: 1 for every session
- Topics_Covered: the abbreviated_title value for that session's paper (e.g. "Tree of Thoughts: Reasoning")

Ensure the file is created at exactly that path. After writing, verify by calling mcp__excel__get_workbook_metadata (should list exactly 2 sheets named Papers and Schedule) and mcp__excel__read_data_from_excel on both sheets to confirm headers, row counts (9 rows including header), and content.

Return: the final path of the file, the confirmed sheet names, and a confirmation that Papers has 8 data rows and Schedule has 8 data rows with the correct headers.
Create Reading_Plan.xlsx

You are creating 8 Google Calendar events for a reading group. Work only within /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-reading-plan-excel-gcal-email/workspace.

STEP 1: Read the staged metadata file at /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-reading-plan-excel-gcal-email/workspace/metadata.json. It is a JSON list of 8 objects, each with keys: assigned_session (1-8), arxiv_id, title (full paper title), abbreviated_title.

STEP 2: Create exactly 8 events using mcp__google_calendar__create_event, one per session (session number = assigned_session). Requirements per event:
- summary (title): "Reading Session N: [abbreviated_title]" where N is the session number and [abbreviated_title] is the abbreviated_title from the metadata (e.g. "Reading Session 4: Tree of Thoughts: Reasoning"). Do not invent abbreviations — use the abbreviated_title value verbatim.
- start: dateTime "2026-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS" with timeZone "UTC", end similarly. Session dates (Mondays, one week apart):
  Session 1: 2026-03-09, Session 2: 2026-03-16, Session 3: 2026-03-23, Session 4: 2026-03-30, Session 5: 2026-04-06, Session 6: 2026-04-13, Session 7: 2026-04-20, Session 8: 2026-04-27.
  Every event: start 10:00 UTC, end 11:30 UTC (e.g. start {"dateTime": "2026-03-09T10:00:00", "timeZone": "UTC"}, end {"dateTime": "2026-03-09T11:30:00", "timeZone": "UTC"}).
- description: must contain the FULL paper title and the arXiv ID, e.g. "Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models\narXiv:2305.10403".

Use each event's returned event ID to confirm creation. After creating all 8, verify with mcp__google_calendar__list_events with timeMin "2026-03-09T00:00:00Z" and timeMax "2026-04-28T00:00:00Z" that exactly 8 events exist, one per Monday, with the correct titles and times.

Return: a list of the 8 created events with their event IDs, titles, start/end times, and confirmation that each description contains the full paper title and arXiv ID.
Create 8 calendar events

You are sending an announcement email for a reading group. Work only within /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-reading-plan-excel-gcal-email/workspace.

STEP 1: Read the staged metadata file at /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-reading-plan-excel-gcal-email/workspace/metadata.json. It is a JSON list of 8 objects, each with keys: assigned_session, arxiv_id, title, abbreviated_title. Use this for accurate paper names.

STEP 2: Send one email using mcp__emails__send_email with these EXACT requirements:
- from_addr: "coordinator@lab.example.com"
- to: "reading-group@lab.example.com"
- subject: MUST contain the phrase "LLM Agent Research Reading Plan" (e.g. "LLM Agent Research Reading Plan: 8-Week Schedule").
- body (plain text): must mention ALL of the following:
  1. The total number of papers: 8.
  2. The date range covered by the reading sessions: sessions run weekly on Mondays from March 9, 2026 through April 27, 2026 (state it as e.g. "March 9 - April 27, 2026" or similar).
  3. The names or topics of AT LEAST THREE of the eight papers. Good candidates from the metadata: "Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools", "Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models", "AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents", "Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection", "Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models", "Mistral 7B", "HuggingGPT: Solving AI Tasks with ChatGPT and its Friends in Hugging Face".
  You may also list all 8 papers for a nicer announcement. Keep the tone professional and warm (a reading group announcement).

After sending, verify the email was sent by searching the Sent folder (mcp__emails__search_emails with query "LLM Agent Research Reading Plan" in folder "Sent", or get the sent folder listing if needed) and confirm the sender, recipient, subject, and that the body contains the required elements.

Return: confirmation of successful send, the subject line used, recipient, and the search result confirming the message exists in the Sent folder.
